rationale: Both reviews independently verify flags/arithmetic against the repo and catch the same headroom-math error, but only X substantively engages the ground-truth theme: it explicitly states 'validation was FL2VA-only' and flags the Ref2VA restart as risky, which is the same underlying fact the human reviewer's 'have we tested reference to va?' question targets. Y instead asserts the recipe 'reports FL2VA/Ref2VA results,' which is inaccurate (the validation table has no Ref2VA row) — a miss on precisely the point ground truth cares about. X also shows deeper independent reasoning (per-layer HBM math, PCIe/NUMA rank derivation, sync-timeout scaling) and better-organized, prioritized actionable fixes, while Y's findings, though grounded, skew toward documentation-completeness nits with some redundancy between its RAM-related findings.
